q: Benchmarks such as SWE-BENCH (Jimenez et al., 2024) have established issue resolution in real-world repositories as a standard evaluation setting
r: EC6: CrossSWE is an SWE-bench-style issue-resolution benchmark (issue to cross-repo patch), so issue repair with no evaluation-method contribution.

q: agents left alone completed an average of 51% of chains
r: Include: BOBA-Bench evaluates agents on 20-request feature chains with eight attempts per chain and strict/regression metrics, an evaluation-method contribution.

q: 22.8% of task–configuration pairs yield inconsistent outcomes across 3 repeated runs
r: Include: benchmark-construction framework plus controlled model-harness comparison with repeated rollouts and variance analysis on developer-requested tasks.

q: We analyze nine benchmarks commonly used to evaluate the effectiveness of agentic coding tools
r: Include: construct-validity analysis of agentic coding benchmarks is a contribution to the evaluation method for coding agents.

q: We independently measure native correctness and persona fulfillment
r: Include: PersonaCodeBench is a new evaluation design (multi-turn coding with simulated personas, separate correctness and personalization measures, cost-performance).

q: Each model is run four times per task
r: Include: Multi-step SWE benchmark of dependent multi-hour feature/migration steps on one repository, with repeated runs and Pass@4, evaluating agent harnesses.

q: We establish a project-takeover evaluation framework combining direct delivery, independent requirement diagnostics, and Oracle state comparisons
r: Include: project-level evaluation of requirement understanding and delivery in existing projects, a new evaluation framework.

q: Repeating an identical configuration accounts for 61% of the variance
r: Include: agents rewrite whole projects, with repetitions, variance decomposition, cost and controls, so the contribution is a controlled evaluation of agent output.

q: A trial is one independent attempt at a task by an agent
r: EC6: Terminal-Bench tasks are terminal-environment tasks, not application code development, so the audit of that benchmark falls outside the kept task types.

q: Each model attempts each task five times
r: Include: EC-SWE has expert-authored multi-file change requests, rubric grading, five runs per model and task with statistical separation analysis.
